title: Grade 9 English — Tenses & Active and Passive Voice
description: Tenses and Active and Passive Voice grammar practice questions
subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct form: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: Simple present tense for third person singular (she/he/it) requires adding -s or -es to the verb. 'She goes' is correct.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
questions.explanation: Past continuous = was/were + V-ing. 'She was eating' describes an action in progress at a past time.

questions.question: The present perfect tense is used for:
options: Actions completed at a specific past time
Past actions with a connection to the present
questions.explanation: Present perfect (have/has + past participle) connects past actions to the present. Example: 'I have finished my homework' (just completed, affects now).

questions.question: Fill in: By the time she arrived, we ___ waiting for an hour.
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous (had been + V-ing) is used for an action that was ongoing over a period before another past event.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I am knowing him for ten years.
I have known him for ten years.
I know him since ten years.
I knew him for ten years ago.
questions.explanation: State verbs like 'know' use present perfect (have known) with 'for' to indicate duration continuing to the present. 'For' is used with a duration; 'since' is used with a point in time.

questions.question: 'He will have completed the project by Monday.' What tense is this?
questions.explanation: Future perfect (will have + past participle) describes an action that will be completed before a specific future time.

questions.question: Identify the tense: 'The sun rises in the east.'
questions.explanation: Simple present tense is used for universal truths, habits, and facts that are always true. 'The sun rises in the east' is a universal truth.

questions.question: Which of the following uses the simple past correctly?
options: Yesterday, she is writing a letter.
Yesterday, she has written a letter.
questions.explanation: Simple past tense is used for completed actions at a specific past time. 'Yesterday' signals past time, and 'wrote' is the simple past form of 'write'.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'The boy kicks the ball.'
options: The ball is kicked by the boy.
The ball was kicked by the boy.
The ball is being kicked the boy.
questions.explanation: Active: Subject + V + Object. Passive: Object + is/are + past participle + by + Subject. 'The boy kicks the ball' → 'The ball is kicked by the boy.'

questions.question: Identify: 'The letter was written by Priya.' This is in:
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the subject receives the action. 'The letter' (subject) receives the action of being written. The doer 'Priya' follows 'by'.

questions.question: Convert to active: 'The match was won by India.'
questions.explanation: Passive 'was won' (past tense) → Active 'won'. Subject of passive 'by India' becomes subject of active. 'India won the match.'

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly in passive voice using past continuous?
options: The cake was being baked by her.
The cake is being baked by her.
The cake had been baked by her.
The cake will be baked by her.
questions.explanation: Past continuous passive = was/were + being + past participle. 'was being baked' is past continuous passive.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'They are building a new school.'
options: A new school is built by them.
A new school was being built.
A new school is being built by them.
A new school has been built by them.
questions.explanation: Present continuous active → passive: Subject + am/is/are + being + V₃ + by + Object. 'is being built by them' is correct.

questions.question: Convert to passive: 'Mother has cooked dinner.'
options: Dinner has been cooked by mother.
Dinner is being cooked by mother.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active (have/has + V₃) → Passive: have/has been + V₃. 'has been cooked by mother' is correct.

questions.question: Which verb form is used in passive voice construction?
questions.explanation: Passive voice always uses the past participle (V₃/3rd form). Pattern: to be + past participle. Example: is written, was eaten, will be done.
